newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Late payments threaten Yugoslavia spring planting.
newsitem.headline: Late payments threaten Yugoslavia spring planting.

text.p: The Yugoslav government's debt to farmers is a serious threat to the country's spring planting campaign, an agriculture ministry official said on Friday.
"The consequences of delayed pay-outs to farmers can be detrimental for this year's spring sowing," agriculture ministry spokesman Milan Prostran told Reuters.
He said the government owed about 350-400 million dinars to farmers for their sugar beet, sunflower and soybean crops.

Association of agricultural cooperatives from the country's bread-basket of Vojvodina on Friday called on their members not to sign any new contracts on spring sowing with processing firms if they were not paid what was owed to them.

"We have agreed not to make any production deals before we collect our debt," said Ljiljana Vasic, president of the association, adding, "While the government is not paying farmers for sugar beet, sunflower and soybean, it has the money for sugar and cooking oil imports."
Prostran said the government must find the money to meet its obligations if it intended to maintain production.
According to the government statistics office, Yugoslavia's 1996 sugar beet production on 70,000 hectares rose 41 percent to 2.4 million tonnes over the previous year.
The sunflower crop jumped 32 percent on the previous year, reaching 389,000 tonnes. The area increased by 34,000 hectares to around 204,000 ha on 1995.

Soybean output in 1996 was up 43 percent over the previous year to around 153,000 tonnes. An additional 21,000 hectares were planted with soybeans in 1996, raising total area under the crop to 73,000 ha.
